facts.statement: Checkout's failing traces end at payment PaymentService/Charge, which returns error.type=Error with 'Invalid token' for loyalty_level=gold. The error propagates to checkout PlaceOrder and frontend (HTTP 422).
Payment logged the same warn-level exception 33 times between 17:14:23 and 17:31:54, with no error-level lines.
Payment's server error ratio rose from 0.0158 at 17:15 to 0.47 at 17:32:44, equal to checkout's ratio at the same time.
PaymentService/Charge is the only checkout client span with errors. Checkout's Charge client errors start at 17:15:42, matching payment's server-side errors.
The flag paymentFailure is ENABLED at variant 50%, and it is the only one of 18 flags that is on.
checkout and payment each have a single revision, created 16:42Z, so there was no rollout near the alert.
Payment's Kubernetes events are all Normal, and payment's Charge p95 latency stays at about 2 ms, so payment is failing with errors, not slowing.
Checkout's own error logs in the window are old Kafka timeouts from 17:06, not the current payment failures.
Cart's EmptyCart client errors reached about 0.56 at 17:07, with a cart server p95 spike up to 15 s, before payment errors began.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check the flagd flag's change history for the turn-on time (expected about 17:14Z). Check whether payment's Charge code reads paymentFailure and whether its failure path matches the 'Invalid token' message.
hypotheses.statement: The paymentFailure flag, enabled at 50%, is what makes payment's Charge reject gold-loyalty requests.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Pull cart server logs and spans for EmptyCart from 17:05 to 17:12Z, checking for exceptions, Valkey timeouts, or pod restarts. Check cart's pod restart and creation metrics, which returned no data.
hypotheses.statement: The earlier cart EmptyCart spike (17:07-17:10Z) is a separate intermittent fault in cart or its valkey-cart backend.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Compare checkout's p95 latency against cart EmptyCart p95 over 17:00-17:31Z, and check whether the latency alert clears when cart latency recovers.
hypotheses.statement: The LatencyP95High alert on checkout is driven by the cart EmptyCart latency spikes rather than by payment, which is not slow.

inferences.statement: Payment's Charge errors are the main driver of checkout's current error budget burn. The failures are partial (about 30-50%), which fits the paymentFailure flag at 50%.
Checkout is not the root cause. Its errors propagate from payment, and its own logs show only old Kafka timeouts.
No recent deployment caused the incident. The current failure is a runtime behavior change in payment, most likely from a flag.

root_causes.cause: Charge rejects gold-loyalty requests with 'Invalid token' at roughly 30-50% of calls, starting about 17:15Z. Most likely the paymentFailure flag at 50%, which is the only enabled flag; not yet confirmed by flag turn-on time or by spans tying the error to the flag.

Intermittent EmptyCart failures and latency spikes (p95 up to 15 s) between 17:07 and 17:10Z, which caused checkout PlaceOrder errors before payment failed. Cause unknown; cart's own error ratio stays low and valkey-cart looks healthy.

diagnosis.summary: checkout's ~26% error rate (0.47 at 17:32) comes from payment's PaymentService/Charge, which rejects requests with 'Invalid token' for loyalty_level=gold. Payment's own server spans show the same error ratio, and payment's latency and pod health are normal. No checkout or payment rollout occurred. The only enabled flag, paymentFailure at 50%, is the most likely deliberate cause, but the flag's turn-on time and its link to the error are not yet confirmed. An earlier, separate cart EmptyCart error and latency spike (17:07-17:10) preceded the payment errors and is not explained.

alternatives.why_not: checkout and payment each have a single revision created 16:42Z, well before the 17:15Z onset, so there is no bad release to roll back to.

payment's latency is normal (about 2 ms), its Kubernetes events are all Normal, and the errors are deterministic per request, so a restart would not clear a flag-driven failure and would only reset a healthy process.
payment is failing with errors, not slowing or saturating, so extra replicas would not reduce the rate of rejected Charge calls.

plan.no_action_reason: The cause is a feature flag (paymentFailure at 50%), which is outside the actions this tool can take. A human should check flagd and disable paymentFailure if it was not meant to be on in this lab. Separately, the cart EmptyCart spike at 17:07-17:10Z and the LatencyP95High alert on checkout are unexplained and need their own investigation of cart and valkey-cart.
plan.summary: Checkout's ErrorBudgetBurn is driven by payment's PaymentService/Charge rejecting gold-loyalty requests ('Invalid token') at about 30-50%, most likely from the paymentFailure flag enabled at 50%. None of rollout_undo, restart_deployment, or scale_deployment addresses a feature flag, so no action is proposed; a human should confirm and disable the flag.

facts.statement: payment's server error ratio rose from about 0.02 at 17:15 to 0.31 at 17:31 and held through 17:36. It was zero before about 17:15.
All payment server errors are on oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge. Request rate stayed flat at about 0.22/s, and payment p95 stayed near 1.9 ms.

20 error traces in 30 minutes show payment's Charge spans failing with 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. demo.user_context.loyalty_level=gold'. The same message propagates to checkout, frontend and frontend-proxy as HTTP 422.
payment logs 31 warn-level lines with that template (thrown at charge.js:48, first 17:14:23Z, last 17:31:39Z). No error-level lines were found.
The flagd flag paymentFailure is ENABLED at variant 50% (value 0.5) with targeting false. flag_state gives no change timestamp.
payment and checkout each have a single revision created 16:42Z, with no restarts or warnings in 120 minutes. flagd has no restarts or warnings either.
checkout's client-side Charge errors toward payment rose from 0.005 at 17:15 to about 0.087 at 17:33, mirroring payment. checkout's Charge p95 stayed around 3.5 to 5.8 ms.
payment's client spans show no error series, and flagd's error ratio stayed near 0.
cart logs 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' 14 to 15 times between 17:02 and 17:31. checkout's slowest trace (4317 ms) spends its time in cart, with EmptyCart at 4290 ms and 1329 ms self time.
checkout's error ratio peaked at 0.31 at 17:07 (POST 0.11, EmptyCart) before falling to about 0 by 17:15 to 17:20. That burst predates payment's errors.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check flagd or flag-config change history for paymentFailure and confirm the flip time is shortly before 17:15Z. Check whether the flag's applicability is limited to loyalty_level=gold, and confirm a flip to OFF restores payment's success ratio.
hypotheses.statement: The paymentFailure flag at 50% is the trigger for payment's errors. Its change time is not confirmed, and 'targeting false' plus a gold-only message needs explaining.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Query kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total for payment and the pod start time for payment-767f6464f-7zl4w, and check the payment logs for startup lines around 17:17Z.
hypotheses.statement: payment restarted around 17:17Z (memory fell from about 137 MB to 68 MB), which may reset in-memory state or a flag cache.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check valkey-cart pod health, connection counts and logs, and cart's Redis client error span attributes. Confirm whether checkout's latency drops after cart recovers.
hypotheses.statement: cart's Redis connection problem is caused by valkey-cart or the network, not by cart itself.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Correlate checkout's 17:07 error spans with kafka and accounting metrics, which returned no series. Check for broker or network issues in kafka.
hypotheses.statement: checkout's 17:07 POST and EmptyCart error burst comes from a separate cause, possibly the Kafka send failures at 17:06Z.

inferences.statement: payment is the origin of the ErrorBudgetBurn on payment and of the checkout Charge-related errors. checkout's own budget burn at 17:31 is mostly propagated from payment.
The failure is a token validation rule inside payment, not a slowdown or a failing dependency. A rollout is ruled out for onset, which points to configuration or flag-driven behaviour.

root_causes.cause: Charge handler rejects a large share of requests with 'Invalid token' for gold-tier users (fast errors, no dependency errors, latency flat). Most likely induced by the paymentFailure flagd flag at 50% (fault injection), not by a rollout, since payment has a single revision from 16:42Z.

Redis/valkey connectivity errors in cart make cart calls slow, which drives checkout's P2 LatencyP95High and its 17:07 POST/EmptyCart error burst. Cart's own error spans are absent, so this is weaker than the payment cause.

diagnosis.summary: payment (lab) is failing about 26-31% of Charge requests with a fast, non-latency 'Invalid token ... loyalty_level=gold' error, starting about 17:15Z. Checkout's payment errors are propagated from payment. The most likely trigger is the paymentFailure flagd flag at 50%, but the flag's change time is unconfirmed and 'targeting false' does not obviously explain a gold-only rule. Checkout's latency and its early 17:07 burst are separate and appear linked to cart's Redis connection errors.

alternatives.why_not: payment has a single revision from 16:42Z, and its errors started around 17:15Z, so there is no earlier release to roll back to.
The errors are deterministic 'Invalid token' rejections for gold-tier users, not a leak or stuck process. The 17:17Z restart did not stop them.
Latency is flat at about 1.9 ms and request rate is steady, so this is not a capacity problem.

plan.no_action_reason: The likely cause is the paymentFailure flagd flag at 50%, and no available action changes flags. A human should check flagd's change history for paymentFailure, set it off or revert it, and confirm payment's error ratio returns to zero. cart's Redis errors are a separate issue to investigate via valkey-cart connectivity.
plan.summary: No rollout, restart, or scale action would fix this. payment's Charge errors look like the paymentFailure flagd fault injection at 50%, which is a flag change, not a deployment change. A human should confirm the flag's change history and disable or revert paymentFailure in flagd.
